overview: Academic labs gain free access to specialized life‑science AI, expanding research capacity
AI agents accelerate antimicrobial peptide discovery, addressing rising drug resistance
Meta’s open‑weight model runs on Macs, highlighting on‑device AI growth

top.title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs
top.summary: OpenAI’s Rosalind Academic Plan offers up to 30 free Business Standard seats for a year, letting eligible labs use GPT‑Rosalind for life‑science tasks, with data not used for model training.

top.title: Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
top.summary: Google DeepMind’s Antigravity platform, using ProtNLM, helped researchers identify a novel antimicrobial peptide from UniProt, now moving to wet‑lab validation to combat resistance.

top.title: Teaching students to think and learn through questions
top.summary: OpenAI launched an AI for Educators course and Study Mode, enabling teachers to use ChatGPT for lesson planning, interactive questioning, and student assessment while preserving pedagogical judgment.

top.title: An update on independent evaluators
top.summary: Anthropic granted METR employee‑level access to its systems for independent risk evaluation, aiming for transparent safety oversight while limiting disclosure of sensitive data.

top.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
top.summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816‑billion‑parameter open‑weight model optimized for Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, targeting multimodal coding and agentic tasks.

top.title: Meta and Apple team up to make Muse AI models run better on Macs
top.summary: Meta and Apple publicly highlighted their collaboration on Muse Spark Open, emphasizing the model’s efficient desktop performance via Apple’s MLX framework on new Mac hardware.
